explanation: Find the middle, split the list, reverse the second half, and weave the halves together. Relinking original nodes produces first, last, second, next-to-last order without changing values.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Splitting separates the original first half from the remaining suffix. Reversing that suffix makes its values appear in last-to-middle order. Alternating one node from each half therefore yields first,last,second,next-to-last and so on. The final middle node is retained once, and only original links change.
walkthrough: For [8,2,7,1,6], keep first half [8,2,7] and reverse second half [1,6] into [6,1]. Weave them to get [8,6,2,1,7], preserving each original node and value.
edgeCases: Empty and singleton lists need no relinking.
Odd lengths retain one final middle node.
The head object and all original node values remain unchanged.
